About Dialpad

Dialpad is the AI platform for customer experience, built to resolve customer problems in real time across voice and digital. Our AI agents learn from your best human agents and improve with every interaction, helping organizations understand their customers, deliver better experiences, increase operational efficiencies, and build a lasting competitive advantage.

Unlike legacy systems built to route and answer, or standalone agentic bot vendors built to deflect, Dialpad was built to resolve. Our AI agents and human agents operate on a single platform with shared context, allowing Agentic AI to resolve issues, advance deals, and eliminate busywork through automation while seamlessly handing conversations to humans when needed, with full context preserved.

Market-leading brands, including Randstad, Motorola Solutions, Netflix, the San Diego Padres, the Colorado Rockies Baseball Club, and Cal Athletics, trust Dialpad. Dialpad is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, GV, ICONIQ Capital, and T-Mobile.

Being a Dialer

At Dialpad, AI isn’t just a feature; it’s how our teams do their best work every day. We put powerful AI tools in every employee’s hands so they can move faster, think bigger, and achieve more.

We believe every conversation matters. And we’ve built the platform that turns those conversations into insight and action, for our customers and ourselves.

We look for people who are intensely curious and hold themselves to a high bar. Our ambition is significant, and achieving it requires a team that operates at the highest level. We seek individuals who embody our core traits: Scrappy, Curious, Optimistic, Persistent, and Empathetic.

Your role

As a Sr. Commercial Counsel, you will serve as a key legal advisor and deal architect for Dialpad's most complex and high-value commercial transactions. You will handle end-to-end negotiation of strategic agreements, provide authoritative guidance on legal risk, and act as a trusted partner to senior business stakeholders across Sales, Finance, Privacy, Security, and Customer Success. You will bring seasoned judgment and independent decision-making to drive deals forward while protecting the company's interests in a fast-moving, global SaaS environment. 

Beyond day-to-day deal work, you will play a key role in helping to shape the commercial legal function itself - building scalable playbooks, embedding AI-powered workflows, mentoring junior counsel, and helping define how the team operates at scale. You will bring an `AI-first` mindset to this work, translating legal expertise into repeatable, technology-enabled systems that improve speed, consistency, and risk management across the organization. 

This position reports to the Deputy General Counsel and has the opportunity to be based in our Austin Office. 

What you’ll do 

Contract Management & Negotiation

- Handle end-to-end negotiation of Dialpad's most significant and complex commercial agreements, including enterprise SaaS agreements, strategic partnership arrangements, reseller and channel agreements, services agreements, and vendor contracts, with minimal supervision.

- Serve as a key point of contact and legal decision-maker for enterprise and strategic accounts, managing deal escalations with sound, risk-calibrated judgment.

- Draft and redline sophisticated contract language across a wide range of commercial terms, including limitations of liability, indemnification, IP ownership, data processing, SLAs, and audit rights.

- Identify, articulate, and resolve complex legal issues with practical, business-oriented recommendations that balance legal risk against commercial objectives.

- Work with outside counsel on real estate leases for Dialpad global offices. 

Cross-Functional Partnership

- Act as a strategic advisor to senior business stakeholders including Sales leadership, Finance, and Customer Success, influencing deal structure and go-to-market strategy from the earliest stages of customer engagement

Eight Sleep’s legal team is one person today: our first in-house legal counsel, who handles everything from IP and litigation to privacy, regulatory, and commercial matters. You’d be the second lawyer, reporting to her, and for a while the team is the two of you.

Your home-base is privacy and regulatory, and there’s a lot of it: the privacy program, FTC and consumer protection, advertising and subscription compliance, product and market-entry questions, and the healthcare-regulatory work that comes with our newer product lines. But this isn’t a role for someone who only wants to live in that lane. What matters most is that you’re willing to take on whatever lands on the department, and that you’re a genuine generalist, just as comfortable picking up a commercial contract, a litigation question, or a product counseling call when that’s what the week calls for.

This is a build role. The company has grown quickly and the legal function is still taking shape, so you’ll be creating programs and processes rather than inheriting them, with a lot of room to own your work. red developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO

We’re looking for a lawyer with 7 + years of practicing attorney experience to join our small and collaborative legal team. The right candidate will have worked at a technology company, be technically savvy and hard-working, keen to learn our products and business, and willing to dig into a wide variety of projects in a fast-paced environment.  On the commercial side, this encompasses complex data in-licenses, as well as customer sales and automotive OEM deals.  Most of our commercial deals involve substantial work with our product and engineering colleagues, so there is a product-counseling aspect to this position as well.

This is a senior individual contributor role where you will come up with practical and creative solutions to get complex deals done and advance our business. Drafting and communication skills are extremely important.  We believe that it is the role of in-house counsel to own the deal. You will develop the ability to both mitigate and accept risk. We almost never say to our colleagues “that’s a business issue for you to decide.”

Mapbox’s customers use our SDKs and APIs to build their own location-aware applications.  Our products are building blocks that our customers can use in various different ways, so our sales agreements are technically more complex than in an enterprise software or SaaS software company.  We don’t believe that lawyers can give good legal advice in a vacuum, so you must be able to become very conversant with and draft agreements based on our specific customers’ use case and technical implementations.  We are not processing hundreds of small sales deals with tweaks to the governing law clause. Instead, our data in-licenses and sales/OEM deals are complex and require a thoughtful approach by a senior lawyer. While we work closely together and thus teach and learn from each other every day, you will not have direct reports.

We think it’s important to continually be improving operational processes/updating forms because this is how we can scale a small legal organization, supporting a fast-growing tech company. You need to share and participate in these efforts to scale our department and improve our services. Prior work in a pre-IPO company will be extremely helpful.

We are a flat organization, but we pitch in and help each other. You must be willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of legal issues, enjoy the give and take of collaboration and take feedback.

The breadth, variety and complexity of projects that you will handle at Mapbox is great training for cross-functional generalists who want to better understand and practically address business problems and risk.




WHAT WE BELIEVE ARE IMPORTANT TRAITS FOR THIS ROLE

 -  7+ years of practicing attorney experience, with 2+ years at a top-tier law firm in any area and 5+ years in-house at a technology company in sales-side commercial transactions (not procurement or privacy/regulatory compliance).

 - At least one of the following is required:
   
   1. Computer engineering, computer science or other similar technical degree.
   
   2. At least 2, but not more than 4, years experience in software patent litigation or patent prosecution at a top tier firm.
   
   3. Extensive experience working with APIs and SDKs.

 - Experience working on complex sales deals.

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced attorney to join our Legal team and support in commercial contracting and development of Payscale's privacy, data, and AI strategy. In this role, you'll drive compliance with evolving global laws in the tech space, advising on product and business initiatives with regulatory implications and helping to build and maintain trust with our customers and partners. You'll work cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Engineering, Information Security, and other business teams to embed compliance-by-design principles across the organization.

What You'll Do

 - Assess customer contracts, vendor contracts and data processing agreements for privacy risks, AI governance requirements, and third-party data sharing restrictions

 - Help maintain corporate policies, terms of service, and related legal documentation in compliance with U.S. and international privacy, data security, and AI laws

 - Conduct risk assessments and advise on data handling practices for new features, integrations, and business initiatives

 - Support the company's response to data subject access requests, deletion requests, incident management, and regulatory inquiries

 - Collaborate cross-functionally to improve relevant processes and implement compliance-by-design principles

 - Monitor the regulatory landscape, advise company leaders regarding new developments, and help implement proactive compliance measures

 - Help develop and deliver trainings for internal teams on core regulatory compliance issues

 - Coordinate with other risk and governance teams on third-party due diligence efforts

We'd love to talk with you if you have:

 - J.D. from an accredited law school and bar admission in at least one U.S. state

 - 3+ years of relevant experience

 - Deep knowledge of GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, the EU AI Act, and other U.S. and international laws applicable to privacy, data security, and AI

 - Experience advising SaaS, data analytics, or technology companies on regulatory compliance matters, with a focus on privacy, data security, and AI

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills with ability to translate complex legal concepts into practical guidance for business audiences

 - Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally

 - Excellent judgment and the ability to independently manage a diverse portfolio of matters

Nice to Have

 - Experience with security frameworks (e.g., SOC 2, FedRAMP)

 - Familiarity with technical concepts related to data security and infrastructure

 - Experience as in-house counsel at a growth-stage technology company

 - Demonstrated interest in leveraging AI tools to improve day-to-day processes

Location

Payscale has an employee centric remote-first model that provides you the flexibility to do your best work in a space that supports you, while also finding time to collaborate in person for the moments that matter.
 
In our remote-first model, employees can work from the location that works best for them. We do not have centralized corporate offices. Employees can choose to work from home, in company-paid co-working spaces, or any combination of the two that best suits their unique needs.

If you work from home, we recommend ensuring that you can meet the following technology, equipment and workspace requirements:

 - High-Speed Internet - A stable broadband or fiber connection (satellite is highly discouraged) with a minimum speed of 100 Mbps in a dedicated workspace that has a reliable Wi-Fi signal.

 - Device for Multifactor Authentication (MFA/2FA) - smartphone, tablet, etc.

When it matters (usually no more than a few times a year) we take the time to gather for in-person events.
